epic.intent:
## Outcome
The generated campaign map follows FWGC++ and can change during play:
- **Biomes.** Terrain looks and behaves like its FWGC++ biome: desert is desert, snow is snow.
- **Smooth terrain.** No spikes, blade ridges or sea cliffs; relief close to vanilla proportions.
- **Magic ground.** Magic-mutated ground is visible, with vanilla-quality textures derived from vanilla and directed by the FWGC++ concept art.
- **Live mutation.** A capital that becomes a magic node changes the surrounding landscape mid-campaign, as computed by FWGC++. Its look and terrain type change, and the change persists in the save.
- **Cities.** Every city FWGC++ generates becomes a town; the world is repaired, never rejected.
- **Villages.** Every town has exactly 3 villages and every castle 2.
- **Nobility.** Kingdoms are made of neighbouring same-civilization realms. Noble family houses, led by FWGC++'s regal people, own the correct cities and castles. Mercenary companies and tavern wanderers are sized to the world at War Sails ratios.
- **Roads.** Roads, including feeder roads to castles and villages, are drawn and speed travel.
- **Settlement looks.** Towns and castles get diverse, culture-correct looks from scaled-down vanilla layouts.
- **Ruins.** FWGC++ ruins are marked on the map.

Research and evidence: `docs/research/map-epic-2-findings.md` (sections are cited in tickets). It was done with REA on the shipped assemblies, plus source reading of MNBL and FWGC++, offline experiments on the real worlds, and an adversarial verifier per topic.

## Owner decisions (2026-10-18)
1. **Clean break.** Pre-epic generated worlds and saves stop loading. One code path everywhere, no legacy readers.
2. **FWGC++ computes mutations.** A planned FWGC++ slice: a `shift_leylines` verb, an `fwg apply` command and a baseline fix.
3. **One early in-game probe**, then the final live test. Nothing else launches the game.
4. **Magic textures are derived from vanilla textures**, with the concept art as direction.
5. **Scaled-down vanilla town and castle layouts** (about 0.5, trimmed to fit), with culture pieces as fallback.
6. **Roads.** A speed bonus and feeder roads to castles and villages. No new bridges beyond the existing decks.
7. **Mutation v1 changes look and terrain type.** It is triggered by an API and debug commands; there is no magic system yet.
8. **Ruins** get a marker per FWGC++ ruin with its name. No gameplay.
9. **"No cities dropped"** means the world FWGC++ generates keeps every city. Repair towns instead of rejecting worlds.
10. **Smooth the terrain** (findings §15).
11. **Noble houses, mercenary companies and wanderers** replace one clan per lord (findings §16).
12. **FWGC++ notable roles stay notables**, except warlords, who become mercenaries.
13. **Targets scale with fief count F at War Sails ratios** (War Sails: 133 fiefs):
    - houses 82·F/133;
    - about 4.95 adult lords per house;
    - the owner's 12 mercenary companies of 6–10 per 133 fiefs;
    - wanderers 35·F/133 (War Sails' start target).
14. **Neighbouring same-civilization realms merge into kingdoms.** Former realm rulers become vassal houses that keep their fiefs. (Default taken; the question was skipped.)
15. **The engine's random child generator stays on**, as in vanilla. At new game it adds about ceil(adults/2) parentless children per house, on top of the planned members.

**Defaults** (findings §14):
- `cold_tundra` gets a Steppe face plus seasonal snow. The Snow face and permanent white go only to `land_ice` and 12-month snow cells.
- Northern-phase seasons everywhere.
- Snow −0.15 and Swamp −0.2 speed terms, with one balance pass.
- Hidden schools reuse a visible school's look.
- FWGC++ zones are frozen after generation.
- Map trees and flora are out of scope.
- Wanderer counts include hired companions, as in vanilla.

## Working rules
- **One sprint. Lean checks:** a ticket is done when it compiles, the existing suites pass (WorldBridge ctest, the managed runner, FWGC++ tests) and new logic has a few targeted assertions.
  - Offline runs are allowed and encouraged: generation, the compile and travel gates on seeds, seam checks, texture gates, terrain-shaping gates, the population census.
  - No per-ticket independent reviews. One review pass happens before the live test.
- **Game launches:** only the early probe ticket and the acceptance node. Acceptance batching: run everything, fix everything in one batch, one confirming run.
- **Shared install (battle-scale session):**
  - CLAIM/OK/RELEASE before any deploy, launch or editor use;
  - check processes first and never touch a process you didn't start;
  - auto-dismiss Safe Mode and crash dialogs;
  - provision grain when campaign time runs;
  - record the `TaleWorlds.Native.dll` and `TaleWorlds.MountAndBlade.dll` hashes. Never restore or re-pin engine binaries.
- **FWGC++ repo** (`C:/Users/davgo/Documents/GitHub/FWGC++`). Generator code is Claude's lane; follow its `AGENTS.md`:
  - write the plan note first;
  - G3: a logged verb;
  - G6: the generator commit before the MNBL consumer;
  - an `api.txt` change goes in its own rule commit;
  - commit with `FWGC_AGENT=claude` through the commit gate; never `--no-verify`;
  - stage files by name; push only when asked.
- **One build, one scene rename.**
  - Every identity-changing piece (policies, projection scale, encoder, face types, settlement builder, population, climate) lands before the live test.
  - The three format bumps share one `requiredCapabilities` id.
  - Re-pin policies once, in dependency order.
- **`travel_graph.cpp` has one owner, serial:** town repair → village quota → feeder roads → face types and road flags. Terrain shaping and the population pass stay out of it.

successCriteria.text: On a generated world, desert, grassland/steppe, forest, marsh, exposed rock, tundra and land ice each render with their own terrain layers from the shared biome table. Land ice stays white all year. Screenshots per biome are recorded.
Navmesh land faces carry the biome's TerrainType from the shared table. Party speed (including the Snow, Swamp and road terms), battle scenes and terrain perks follow it in game.
Seasonal snow follows FWGC++'s snow season. Advancing to winter whitens the regions FWGC++ snows on, and the gameplay Snowy fraction matches the snow-season length.
All 8 visible magic schools have vanilla-derived ground texture sets that pass the review gates. The world's generated magic variants are visible on the map.

A debug-cast fire event at a capital runs FWGC++ `fwg apply` in the background and changes nearby ground. Look, terrain type and battle scene all change. The mutation survives save and Continue, no generator process runs during the load, and navigation caches are reused.

Every FWGC++ city becomes a town (same uid set at every stage, and the in-game Town count matches). No world is rejected for an unplaceable or unreachable town. A 20-seed offline sweep records accept and attempt-0 rates.
Every town has exactly 3 bound villages and every castle 2. All ports survive and no fortification has 0 villages.
FWGC++ routes plus feeder roads connect every town, castle and village to the network within its land group. They are drawn on the map with bridges at the existing decks and give a road speed bonus.
Towns and castles use culture-correct looks from scaled vanilla layouts. Nearest neighbours avoid the same look where the pool allows, and the siege contract still holds.
Each FWGC++ ruin has a map marker with its name, and a ruins encyclopedia page lists them.
The single live test ran on the shared install under the CLAIM/RELEASE rules, with the native DLL hashes recorded. The clean break is documented in docs/save-compatibility.md.

Terrain on worlds A and B meets the smoothing gates: interior slope p95 ≤ 45° and max ≤ 60°, coast p95 ≤ 50°, no isolated spikes, at most 10 settlement pads over 25°, no lake newly hidden. Travel classes match the pre-smoothing compile, and in-game screenshots show no blade ridges or sea cliffs.

At game start on each world, kingdoms are merged neighbouring same-civilization realms. Noble houses number about 82·F/133, with 3–10 planned members each, about 4.95 adult lords on average, and at least one adult of each sex. The engine's random children come on top and are counted separately. Every fief is owned by a house of its kingdom, and each castellan heads or belongs to the house owning its castle. There are about 12·F/133 mercenary companies of 6–10 heroes and about 35·F/133 wanderers. Every living FWGC++ hero is in exactly one bucket or is a notable.

epic.title: Map epic 2: biome terrain, magic mutation, roads, settlements

bundle.rationale:
## Shape
One sprint, 19 work tickets plus the acceptance node (MMR-247). Testing is lean, with one exception the owner approved: a short early in-game probe (MMR-249). It settles the native unknowns that the terrain, snow, decal, texture, overlay and terrain-resolution work rests on.

## Order
- **MMR-248 first.** It freezes one shared biome table and every new policy key (including terrain shaping, the projection scale and population), so faces, layers, battle classes, colour grade and the mutation remap agree. It also re-pins once.
- **The travel compiler has one owner, run in series:** MMR-251 town repair → MMR-252 village quota → MMR-253 feeder roads → MMR-254 face types. Face types must classify the final classes.
- **Terrain smoothing** follows the probe and feeds the layer compile (MMR-255), which uses shaped slopes for rock. MMR-256 (climate) follows.
- **The population pass** runs after the village quota, then its emitters and runtime ticket.
- **The FWGC++ slice (MMR-250)** runs in parallel in its own repo under its gates. It lands before the MNBL consumer (MMR-261), per G6.
- **Textures (MMR-259)** feed the magic overlay (MMR-260), which feeds the runtime mutation (MMR-261).
- **One review pass (MMR-262)**, then one integrated live test (MMR-247).

## Highest risks
- Native behaviour of more than 2 layers, decals, dynamic snow and level-7 terrain. The probe covers it.
- Texture quality.
- Settlement density: generated towns are about 4.5× closer than vanilla.
- FWGC++ lifting its age-boundary rule.
- Seed 42 passing the village quota only through the tightest tier.
- Small kingdoms dissolving under conquest; merging realms reduces this.
- Wanderer and mercenary template limits: few female templates, all-male leader refills.

The clean break removes all legacy-path work.

exitCriteria.text: The acceptance live test passed after at most one fix batch and one confirming run. Its results are in evidence/map-epic-2/acceptance.json and docs/research/map-epic-2-findings.md.

sprints.goal: The generated map follows FWGC++. Biome terrain looks and behaves right, magic ground is visible and mutates live, every city survives, villages are 3 per town and 2 per castle, roads are drawn, settlement looks vary and ruins are marked. Everything is proven in one live test.

acceptanceCriteria.text: MMR-248's shared table governs faces, layers, battle classes and the mutation remap in the build that ran.
MMR-249's probe decisions (delivery mode, decal technique, compositing, scale, 513 go/no-go) are the ones the build used.
FWGC++ `fwg apply` from the re-pinned producer computed the live mutation.
Both worlds kept every FWGC++ city: the in-game Town count equals sites, with the same uids.
Both worlds show exactly 3 villages per town and 2 per castle in game, with ports intact.
Every settlement is reached by a drawn road (routes and feeders).
Face types follow biomes in game, and the speed tooltip shows the Snow, Swamp, Forest, Desert and road terms.
Each biome renders with its layers (screenshots), and land ice stays white.
Winter whitens FWGC++ snow regions, and the Snowy gameplay state follows season length.
Road decals, bridges at decks and ruin markers render, and the ruins page lists every ruin.
Towns and castles show culture-correct scaled vanilla layouts with intact siege visuals.
The magic ground textures render from the published packs, and the owner has reviewed them.
Generated magic variants are visible, and the overlay drives terrain type and battle scenes.
The fire cast mutates nearby ground live and persists through save and Continue, with no generator process at load and nav caches reused.
The review pass findings were fixed or deferred with a reason before the first live run.
The run followed CLAIM/RELEASE, recorded the native DLL hashes and left the install as found. evidence/map-epic-2/acceptance.json records each step as pass, fail, blocked or not-run.
In-game screenshots of mountains and coasts on world 1 show smoothed relief with no blade ridges or sea cliffs, and settlements sit on level pads.

The day-0 census on both worlds matches the compiled population (kingdoms, houses and sizes, fief owners, companies, wanderers). The engine's random child generator ran without errors, adding about ceil(adults/2) children per house.
In game, houses and companies appear as compiled. Mercenary clans are minor clans with their heroes flagged, and wanderers keep their FWGC++ names and sex.
After 30+ days wanderers stay at W (hired included), companies keep 4 or more heroes, and an AI kingdom hires a company. House and kingdom changes are recorded.

reasoning.rationale: One integrated live run with a single fix batch.

tickets.title: Run the one early in-game probe

acceptanceCriteria.text: `shift_leylines` and `fwg apply` exist with passing FWGC++ tests, and landed through the commit gate in the required commit order (rule commit, generator commit).
A zero-edit apply on seed 42 size 129 produces an empty delta.

tickets.title: FWGC++: shift_leylines verb, fwg apply and a fresh baseline

acceptanceCriteria.text: In the 20-seed sweep no world is rejected for unplaceable_town or unreachable_town, and every repair is recorded per town.
The preservation assertion holds for every accepted world. The sweep's accept and attempt-0 rates are recorded in evidence/fwg/city-preservation.json.

tickets.body:
Findings §11.

**The problem.** One unplaceable or unreachable town rejects the whole world (`travel_graph.cpp:670-682`, `:695-715`) and a derived seed replaces it.
- 30 of 31 seeds were rejected.
- At that rate a random seed loses every city about 90% of the time.

**Work:**
- **Bounded town repairs** in the travel compiler:
  - a towns-only larger snap radius;
  - carve a land cell under the town;
  - join an unreachable town's group with a pass or deck, or give an island town a forced port.

  Towns stay unexcludable (`campaign_compiler.cpp:578`). Record each repair per town uid.
- **Keep the requested seed** when the cause was repairable. Record every attempt's city count in the generation record.
- **Preservation assertion** in the generation driver and the bundle validator: sites = `placed_cities` = compiled towns = travel towns = id-map towns, with the same uid set.
- **Fix MNBL stale wording:** `campaign-content.json` notes and `campaign-semantics.md:124`.

**Offline check:** run generation and the quality gate on seeds 42–61 at size 129. Record accept rate, attempt-0 rate and town counts in `evidence/fwg/city-preservation.json`.
tickets.title: Repair towns instead of rejecting worlds

acceptanceCriteria.text: On seeds 42 and 73 (size 129) every town has exactly 3 and every castle exactly 2 bound villages. All ports are kept and no fortification has 0 villages.
Determinism and pass-2 stability tests pass, and campaign.json v2 records origin, sourceTown and the villageQuota block.
VillageBinding passes v2 through, and SettlementFactory validates exactly 3/2.

tickets.body:
Findings §9. Add a WorldBridge pass `village_quota.cpp` inside `travel::run`, after placement. `compile()` stays faithful to the source.

**Steps:**
1. **Pin ports.** Each port town's chosen harbour village stays with its town.
2. **Keep 3 per town.** Preference order:
   - the pinned village;
   - at most one more harbour village;
   - land villages that diversify production;
   - then the nearest.
3. **Castles** take their 2 nearest villages from their garrison town.
4. **Reassign surplus** to short fortifications, own kingdom first.
5. **Drop the rest** with a `quota:` exclusion that doesn't count toward the travel cap. Notables move as today.
6. **Synthesize** missing villages on Land cells of the fortification's land component:
   - clearance tiers **scaled by town spacing S**;
   - uid `mnbl-quota-village:<fort uid>:<n>`, a unique name, `cultureUid`, a role.
7. **Second analysis pass** with the pass-1 repaired classes frozen. Assert stable ports and no new exclusions.
8. **Fallbacks.** Never reject a world for the quota:
   - islet towns use the tightest tier;
   - a castle that still can't be filled is excluded with a recorded reason (last resort).

**Also change:**
- `campaign.json` v2: `bound` (town or castle), `sourceTown`, `origin`, tier and a `villageQuota` block.
- `closure_problems` and `exclude()` accept castle-bound villages.
- `VillageBinding` passes v2 through.
- `SettlementFactory.Validate` requires exactly 3/2.
- Graph validation rules and the preview follow.

**Never** produce a fortification with 0 villages: vanilla `SnareTheWealthy` and `incident_the_quiet_life` crash on it.

reasoning.rationale: Two analysis passes, synthesis with clearance tiers, and closure rules.

tickets.title: Exactly 3 villages per town and 2 per castle

acceptanceCriteria.text: On seeds 42 and 73 every town, castle and village connects to the road network within its land group, recorded in travel-graph.json.
Road cells are deterministic and seam/pole safe in WorldBridge tests.

tickets.body:
Findings §8. FWGC++ roads are a minimum spanning forest between cities only, and 7 of world A's 45 cities have no road.

**Work:**
- **Use the exact route lattice** the compiler already rasterizes:
  - split routes at poles (world B route 58);
  - skip `sameGroup=false` sea legs;
  - treat road passes as road land.
- **Generate feeder roads** along land travel cells (cheapest path; passes allowed):
  - from every final castle and village (after the MMR-252 quota) to its bound settlement;
  - from road-less cities to the nearest road or town in their land group.

  Feeder roads never create a new water crossing; no new decks.
- **Emit** `roads[]` with cell paths and kind (route or feeder) into `travel-graph.json` (schema update), plus a per-cell road flag for `cells.bin` v2, whose format MMR-254 writes.
tickets.title: Feeder roads and road cells in the travel compiler

acceptanceCriteria.text: Navmesh faces on seeds 42 and 73 follow the shared table (per-type histograms recorded), and the validator passes offline.
The speed model chain is Road → Naval → Default with the policy factors, covered by unit assertions.
A test asserts that no navigation-cache key input depends on anything mutable.

tickets.title: Biome face types, road flags and one speed model

acceptanceCriteria.text: Seeds 42 and 73 compile with N layers. Per-layer coverage matches the shared table, and the seam check passes on every plane.
The template is generated from tracked source and has no flora on weighted layers.
WorldBridge ctest, the surface tests and the managed runner pass.

reasoning.rationale: Encoder, compiler and template change together, and must keep the C++/Python parity.

tickets.title: Compile biome terrain layers

acceptanceCriteria.text: The node-level Snowy fraction follows FWGC++'s snow-season length on seed 42 (offline assertion).
Map load binds the snow texture and drives the season threshold; a log row records both.
docs/water-climate.md and docs/runtime-capabilities.md are updated.

tickets.body:
Findings §5, using MMR-249's binding answers and MMR-255's template.

**Gameplay byte:**
- The snow byte comes from snow-season length through the inverse installed formula (196 = 12 months … 30 = peak only); `ice_cap` → 255.
- Test at node level under the real `PeriodicWorldCoordinates` layout.

**Visuals:**
- An RGBA visual snow raster (R snow, G rain).
- Bind it with `Texture.CreateFromByteArray` + `Scene.SetDynamicSnowTexture` at map load, on the thread MMR-249 proved; release it on teardown.
- Never call the vanilla binder or `GetPixelData`.

**Colour grade:**
- Add a runtime `MapColorGradeManager` (or our own per-tick `SetTerrainDynamicParams`).
- Split the grade grid's grassland by moisture and mode-filter it.
- Update `WorldSurfaceProbe`.

**Identity and docs:** one climate identity bump (clean break). Fix the "no safe creation path" docs.
tickets.title: Snow seasons, dynamic snow and a runtime colour grade

acceptanceCriteria.text: Road decals, bridges and ruin markers are built from bundle data and removed on teardown. Counts are asserted offline from the builders.
The ruins encyclopedia page lists every FWGC++ ruin of the world, with name, civilization and cause.

tickets.body:
Findings §8 and §11, using MMR-249's decal technique.

**Roads:**
- Decals along smoothed MMR-253 road paths, in per-culture families (empire, khuzait, battania), clipped at gates.
- Nearest-image refresh at the seam.
- Lifetime tracking and removal on world release.

**Bridges:**
- Prefabs (`map_bridge_b/c/d/e`) at the existing decks, read from the kept `navigation.json` `build.bridges` (installed-scene loads skip `Prepare`).
- z from bank ground; a yaw rule that covers L-shaped decks (skip or rotate); a measured scale.

**Ruins:**
- Read FWGC++ `ruins[]`: name, civilization, cause, age, node.
- Place one marker entity per ruin (vanilla ruin pieces), with its name on hover.
- Add a custom encyclopedia page listing every ruin. No gameplay.
tickets.title: Draw roads, bridges and ruin markers

acceptanceCriteria.text: On seeds 42 and 73 every town and castle gets a culture-correct look. Nearest neighbours avoid the same look where the pool allows, with a report.
The baked scene passes the relaxed contract checks offline, with no nested prefab references and no solid colliders.
Entity count and scene size per world are recorded.

reasoning.rationale: Scene XML normalization, fitting and the siege contract.

tickets.title: Diverse settlement looks from scaled vanilla layouts

acceptanceCriteria.text: Eight school texture sets plus decal atlases pass the gates, recorded in evidence/art/magic-textures.json.
The published packs load by name (header check) and are referenced by the overlay or the template.

tickets.body:
Findings §6 (owner decision 4: derived from vanilla). Uses MMR-249's tile scale and delivery choice.

**Inputs and spec:**
- Fix the `.tpac` extractor: raw chunks, and the large packs for snow, ice and stone_desert.
- Settle the spec contradictions: `_h` vs `ground_slope_scale`, parents per core, gloss caps, minimum accent size.

**Production:**
- A derivation tool with recipes for the 8 visible schools; hidden schools reuse visible looks.
- Material language from the FWGC++ concept art and briefs; weave is matched against the approved concept art.
- Macro identity at map zoom, not patterns inside the tile.
- A decal stamp atlas per school with baked falloff.
- Prototype starting point: scratch `wf5/magicground2.py`.

**Gates:**
- macro ΔE ≥ 10 vs the parent and the neighbouring biome layers;
- vanilla stat envelopes;
- seams;
- a BCn round-trip.

**Publish:**
- Import into `Modules/MNBL.ProceduralWorld/AssetSources` with the vanilla flags.
- Publish through the Modding Kit: try the console `publish` command first, otherwise one owner-performed editor step under CLAIM/RELEASE.
- Verify the published headers.
- Packs are release inputs (LFS); update `config/mods.json`.
- Reference vanilla `_n`/`_s` by name where unchanged.

reasoning.rationale: Art derivation with quality gates, plus an editor publish step.

tickets.title: Magic-mutation ground textures

acceptanceCriteria.text: Seed 42's generated magic variants are drawn (decal or layer count recorded) and agree with the shared table.
Unit tests show face overrides only within the land-valid set, and battle-index patches covering every strip image.
The navigation-cache key is unaffected by the overlay (assertion).

tickets.body:
Findings §7, consumer side.

**`WorldSurfaceOverlay`:**
- base `biome_variant` read from the source `world.json` (optional magic layers, so magic-off worlds still load) plus mutation cells;
- physical → source mapping that covers the seam and pole rows;
- an immutable snapshot, swapped atomically.

**Visuals**, per MMR-249's choice:
- (A) decals for all magic ground with MMR-259's textures, scaled by potency; or
- (B) MMR-255's baked school layers for generated variants plus same-texture decals for mutations.

In both cases:
- node effects (particle and point light) as separate root entities, not inside baked settlements;
- colour-grade cells (MMR-256's manager);
- every periodic image;
- teardown.

**Gameplay:**
- `GeneratedMapScene` redeclares `GetFaceTerrainType`, `GetTerrainTypeAtPosition` and `GetEnvironmentTerrainTypes(Count)` over a per-face override.
- Build the override before `MobileParty.PreAfterLoad` / `ComputePathAfterLoad`.
- Remap only within the land-valid set, per MMR-248's table; never change passability.
- Patch the battle index map in every strip image.
- No allocation on the hot path.

reasoning.rationale: Hot-path overlay with load ordering, seam images and visuals.

tickets.title: Magic ground overlay and live terrain-type overlay

acceptanceCriteria.text: Offline: a recorded `fwg apply` delta for a fire cast at Nerdun applies to the overlay and round-trips through SyncData byte-identically.
A test shows no generator process can start during a load.
A test shows a producer change refuses new casts while stored mutations still load.

tickets.body:
Findings §7, MNBL side (owner decisions 2 and 7). This is the MNBL consumer commit, after MMR-250 lands in FWGC++ (G6).

**Inputs:**
- Store the accepted `request.json` in each bundle.
- Re-pin `fwg.exe` with `apply`: `producer.lock.json`, capabilities and help hashes.

**Trigger:**
- `WorldMutations.Report(MagicEvent{school, settlement, strength})` plus console commands (cast, list).
- A daily batch keeps per-(site, school) residue. When a threshold is crossed it emits a `LeylineEdit` at the capital: the FWGC++ capital the kingdom still holds, else the ruler clan's home.

**Compute:**
- Run `fwg apply` on a background thread during play, **never during a load** (the process audit).
- Apply results on the engine thread at a safe point; cancel on world release.

**Persist:**
- One string `SyncData` key with canonical JSON: producer sha, edits, changed cells, digest, pending queue.
- Load replays the stored cells only.
- On a digest mismatch, keep the log, disable the overlay and block casts.
- Ledger entries, an `mnbl.campaign.*` header key, saveIds v2.
- After a producer change, new casts are refused and stored mutations still load.

Feed results to MMR-260's overlay. No decay in v1.

reasoning.rationale: Background process, engine-thread handoff and save persistence.

tickets.title: Runtime landscape mutation

acceptanceCriteria.text: Every finding of the single review pass is fixed or explicitly deferred with a reason in the ticket result.

tickets.title: One review pass before the live run

acceptanceCriteria.text: Worlds A and B pass every offline gate, recorded in evidence/fwg/terrain-shaping.json.

Synthetic CTests pass: a spike is removed, a ridge is kept, the slope bound holds, sea, lake and river samples are handled per the spec, pole rows stay single-valued, seams are identical, two compiles are byte-identical, and a bad policy is refused. Python parity has z error 0.
Every absolute-height consumer of the old 0.01 scale is updated, and the managed runner passes.

reasoning.rationale: Heightfield shaping with navigation, lakes, seam and parity constraints.

tickets.title: Smooth the campaign terrain

acceptanceCriteria.text: On seeds 42 and 73 kingdoms are contiguous same-civilization merges within the policy maximum. Houses, adult lords, companies and wanderers match the War Sails-scaled targets within ±10%, with houses at 3–10 planned members and companies at 6–10.

Every fief is owned by a house of its kingdom and no house holds more than 4. Each castellan heads or belongs to its castle's owner house. Every house has an adult of each sex and a vanilla lord culture. Every living FWGC++ hero is in exactly one bucket or is a notable, with 0 unassigned.
A re-run is byte-identical, house and company names are unique without numerals, the census matches the evidence file, and WorldBridge ctest passes.

reasoning.rationale: Kingdom merging, house formation, kin synthesis and bucket accounting over real FWGC++ data.

tickets.title: Plan kingdoms, noble houses, mercenary companies and wanderers

acceptanceCriteria.text: Generated documents for seeds 42 and 73 contain the merged kingdoms, the planned houses and minor mercenary clans (owner set, templates resolve, town homes, unique colour pairs), house and company Lords with kin links, and the planned wanderers.
SettlementFactory and CampaignGraphValidator pass with house owners and homes. Minors are accepted only with both parents set, and dead parents are excluded from the census.
The managed test runner passes with the new census tests, and the docs are updated.

acceptanceCriteria.text: It builds, the managed runner passes, and the patch descriptor resolves against the installed TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.dll (checked offline).

tickets.body:
Runtime side of findings §16.

- **Engine children (kept).** `InitialChildGenerationCampaignBehavior` stays on, as in vanilla.
  - Generated lords are XML heroes, so they exist before it runs and are counted.
  - Nothing MNBL creates later is assigned to a house before it runs.
  - Mark it "retained" in `campaign-compatibility.json`.
- **Mercenary flag.** Set `Hero.IsMinorFactionHero = true` on every company member at the earliest new-game hook, before minor-clan parties spawn if possible. MMR-262 checks the timing. Re-assert it on load.
- **Wanderers.** One Harmony prefix on `CompanionsCampaignBehavior.DailyTick`, with a v1.4.8 signature check like the existing descriptors:
  - keep `SwapCompanions`;
  - never run `TryKillCompanion`;
  - top up only when fewer than W Wanderer-occupation heroes are alive (hired included);
  - the top-up re-implements creation (`CreateSpecialHero` from a chosen template + `EnterSettlementAction`) with an FWGC++-style name, culture and sex. The vanilla method can't take a template.
  - Count heroes, not templates.
  - Don't patch the private `get__desiredTotalCompanionCount` (JIT inlining risk).
- **Compatibility statuses:** CompanionsCampaignBehavior daily tick replaced; HeroSpawnCampaignBehavior kept (companies start with 4 or more heroes).
- **Kingdom discontinuation.** Kept as vanilla, and documented: merged kingdoms make it rarer.
- **Census.** `CampaignSoakProbe` takes a census at day 0 and after 30+ days: kingdoms, houses and sizes, engine children per house (separate), minor clans, `IsMinorFactionHero`, wanderers (free and hired). MMR-247 runs it.
